questions.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $1$st row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+3\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{14} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+1\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3+2 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|=3\cdot 5=15.
$$

questions.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| & =4\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+0\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{4+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-4|\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot {C}_{21}+0\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(9-2) \\  & =-14\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|=-4\cdot (-14)=56.
$$

$$

Now, computing the first $3\times 3$  determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =(-1)\cdot {C}_{21}+2\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{2+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2-3)+2(1-3) \\  & =-5+2\cdot (-2) \\  & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute the second $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along its $3$rd row:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{31}+1\cdot {C}_{32}+1\cdot {C}_{33} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{3+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(4-2)+(-2+1) \\  & =-2+(-1) \\  & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|=-2\cdot (-9)+3\cdot (-3)=18-9=9.

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{21}+(-1)\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23}+1\cdot {C}_{24} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{2+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the first $3\times 3$  determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+2\cdot {C}_{12}+(-1)\cdot {C}_{13} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{1+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot (-1)^{1+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(6-2)-(-6-2) \\  & =-8-(-8) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute the second $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{11}+1\cdot {C}_{12}+2\cdot {C}_{13} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}|+(2)\cdot (-1)^{1+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(-6-2)+2(0-6) \\  & =-(-8)+2\cdot (-6) \\  & =8-12 \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -4 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}|=-0+(-4)=-4.
